body.statement:
At every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), let every training fold use the support-cleaned coherent fit and the data-driven Gram inverse at \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\).  Suppose, for every fold,
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1),
 \qquad \tau_{S,n}=o_P(n^{-1/4}),
 \qquad R_\Sigma=o_P(1),
 \qquad \Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Then
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)\rightsquigarrow N(0,V_{\mathrm{eff}}),
\]
and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  The raw matrices \(\widehat M_A,\widehat M_Z\) are used only to construct \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\) and the screening ratio; all bridges, posterior objects, projectors, and scores use the cleaned matrices.
body.justification: The attaining theorem now exposes the exact screening, random-threshold, stability, and quadratic-bias conditions required by the non-oracle cleaned estimator.
body.gap: Prior hidden-treatment limit theorems do not combine the exact multilevel projector with support cleaning and a data-driven Gram rank.
body.consumer: It yields efficient standard errors for latent maternal-smoking exposure means when the declared rate conditions are verified.
body.proof_tex:
For a training fold \(f\), define
\[
 S(O)=U(O)-QU(O)=\psi+\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O),
 \qquad
 \widehat S_f=\widehat U_f-\widehat Q_f\widehat U_f,             \tag{80}
\]
where every hatted object in \(\widehat S_f\) is computed from the cleaned product law.  Let \(n_f\) be the size of its held-out fold.  Adding and subtracting foldwise conditional means gives the exact decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n(\widehat\psi-\psi)
={}&n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)\\
&+n^{-1/2}\sum_{f=1}^{F_{\mathrm{fold}}}
 \sum_{i:\,\mathrm{fold}(i)=f}
 \bigl[(\widehat S_f-S)(O_i)-P(\widehat S_f-S)\bigr]\\
&+n^{-1/2}\sum_{f=1}^{F_{\mathrm{fold}}}n_fP(\widehat S_f-\psi). \tag{81}
\end{aligned}
\]
Conditional on the training observations for fold \(f\), its held-out observations are independent of \(\widehat S_f\), and its centered summands have conditional second moment bounded by
\[
 \frac{n_f}{n}\|\widehat S_f-S\|_2^2.                          \tag{82}
\]
The cleaned score-stability lemma and \(R_\Sigma=o_P(1)\) make (82) converge to zero in probability.  Conditional Markov inequality and the fixed number of folds therefore make the middle two lines of (81) \(o_P(1)\).

The support-cleaning event has probability tending to one because \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\).  On that event the quadratic-bias lemma gives, foldwise,
\[
 \left\|n^{-1/2}\sum_fn_fP(\widehat S_f-\psi)\right\|
 \leq\sqrt n\,C_{\mathrm{reg}}\max_f\Delta_{n,f}=o_P(1).       \tag{83}
\]
The explicitly imposed condition \(\tau_{S,n}=o_P(n^{-1/4})\) covers training-fold-random thresholds and ensures that the cleaning contribution \(r_A^c-r_A=r_Z^c-r_Z=\tau_{S,n}\) lies in the required product-rate window; the actual bias conclusion in (83) is recorded by \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\).  Equations (81)--(83) prove the asymptotic linear expansion.

The true regularity margins, bounded outcome, fixed \(K\), and the finite-projector and Gram-gap bounds make \(\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}\) bounded and centered.  For fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^K\), Taylor expansion of its characteristic function, with a bounded third-order remainder, gives
\[
 E_P\exp\{it^{\mathsf T}\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}V_{\mathrm{eff}}t}{2n}+o(n^{-1}).       \tag{84}
\]
Independence raises (84) to the \(n\)-th power, whose limit is
\(\exp\{-t^{\mathsf T}V_{\mathrm{eff}}t/2\}\).  Thus every scalar projection has the asserted normal limit, and the characteristic function identifies the joint limit as \(N(0,V_{\mathrm{eff}})\).  Combining this limit with the asymptotic linear expansion proves the second assertion.

For covariance consistency, score stability gives \(\widehat S_f\to S\) in \(L^2(P)\) for every fold.  The fitted half-margins, spectral cutoff, and bounded outcome make these scores uniformly bounded.  Conditional on the training data, a direct second-moment calculation therefore gives
\[
 \left\|P_{n,f}(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})
 -P(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})\right\|_{\mathrm F}=o_P(1). \tag{85}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|P(\widehat S_f\widehat S_f^{\mathsf T})-P(SS^{\mathsf T})\|_{\mathrm F}
 \leq\|\widehat S_f-S\|_2(\|\widehat S_f\|_2+\|S\|_2)=o_P(1). \tag{86}
\]
Summing the fixed number of folds and using the already proved consistency \(\widehat\psi\to_P\psi\) yields
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}
 \to_P E_P\{(S-\psi)(S-\psi)^{\mathsf T}\}=V_{\mathrm{eff}},
\]
as required.
